claude.sample_unit: subjects (15 epilepsy, 15 healthy) in external scalp-EEG cohort

links.outcome: Accuracy with subject overlap versus strict patient-independent partitions
links.effect: Permitting subject overlap elevated accuracy to 59%-96%, whereas strict patient separation reduced it to 41%-53% in 95% CI.
links.quote: Permitting subject overlap artificially elevated accuracy to 59%-96%, whereas strict patient separation reduced it to 41%-53% in 95% Confidence Interval.

links.outcome: Performance drop from benchmark dataset to new clinically verified external cohort
links.effect: Overall accuracy fell from ⩾94% on the benchmark dataset to 42%-53% on the external cohort; sensitivity as low as 0.97% for the deep CNN.
links.quote: When transferred unchanged to the external cohort, overall accuracy fell from⩾94% on the benchmark dataset to 42%-53%, with sensitivities as low as 0.97% for the deep convolutional neural network and specificities dropping to 4% for time-frequency methods.

screen.practice: external validation with patient-independent data partitioning
screen.reason: The study empirically tests the clinical readiness and generalizability of five EEG diagnostic models via external validation and directly measures the effect of patient-independent partitioning versus subject-level data leakage.

primary.practice: external validation and patient-level data leakage prevention
